stem: A manufacturing study measures defect rate across 3 factorys, each containing multiple production lines. factory A has 10 observations with mean 67.5 % (within-factory SD = 8.9). factory B has 8 observations with mean 89.9 % (within-factory SD = 7.9). factory C has 8 observations with mean 70.5 % (within-factory SD = 6.0). The between-factory standard deviation is uncertain, estimated between 8.8 and 22.0 %. Using a hierarchical Bayesian model, estimate the true defect rate for factory B, accounting for shrinkage toward the grand mean and the uncertainty in the between-factory variation.

ground_truth.answer: Hierarchical estimate for factory B: 89.4 % (shrunk from raw 89.9). Range [88.6, 89.7] as between-factory SD varies from 8.8 to 22.0. Pooled mean: 75.3.

solution_steps: Compute pooled (grand) mean: 75.3 % (weighted average of 3 factory means).
Shrinkage factor for factory B: B = σ²_between / (σ²_between + σ²_within/8). At σ_between=14.7: B = 0.965.
Interval [88.6, 89.7] captures uncertainty from the unknown between-group variance.
common_failure_modes: Using the raw observed mean (89.9) without shrinkage
Using only the grand mean (75.3) and ignoring group-specific data
Not recognizing that small-sample groups should be shrunk more toward the grand mean
Treating the between-group variance as known rather than uncertain
